functional.title: Verify API documentation page is accessible and loads correctly
preconditions: User is logged into the application with a valid account
API documentation has been published and deployed to the documentation portal
User has at least 'Viewer' or 'Developer' role permissions
Browser is a supported version (Chrome 90+, Firefox 88+, Edge 90+, Safari 14+)

steps.action: Navigate to the main application dashboard and locate the 'Documentation' or 'API Docs' link in the top navigation bar or sidebar menu
steps.expectedResult: A 'Documentation' or 'API Docs' navigation link is visible and clickable

steps.action: Click on the 'API Documentation' link
steps.expectedResult: The API documentation page loads within 3 seconds, displaying the documentation landing page with a table of contents, API overview section, and version information

steps.action: Verify the page structure includes sections for: Introduction, Authentication, Endpoints, Request/Response formats, Error codes, and Rate limiting
steps.expectedResult: All major sections are present in the table of contents and are navigable via anchor links or sidebar navigation

steps.action: Scroll through the entire API documentation page from top to bottom
steps.expectedResult: All content renders correctly without broken layouts, missing images, or placeholder text. Code examples are properly formatted with syntax highlighting

steps.action: Check the API version number displayed on the documentation page
steps.expectedResult: The API version number is clearly displayed (e.g., 'API v1.0' or similar) and matches the current deployed API version

postconditions: API documentation page remains loaded and accessible for continued browsing
User session remains active and authenticated
No console errors related to documentation rendering appear in browser developer tools

functional.title: Verify user guide is accessible and contains all required sections
preconditions: User is logged into the application with a valid account
User guide documentation has been published and is available in the documentation portal
User has at least 'Viewer' role permissions

steps.action: Navigate to the documentation portal and click on the 'User Guide' section link
steps.expectedResult: The User Guide landing page loads successfully, displaying a title, introduction paragraph, and a structured table of contents

steps.action: Review the table of contents for the following sections: Getting Started, Account Setup, Core Features, Configuration, Troubleshooting, and FAQ
steps.expectedResult: All expected sections are listed in the table of contents with clickable links to each section

steps.action: Click on the 'Getting Started' section link in the table of contents
steps.expectedResult: The page scrolls to or navigates to the 'Getting Started' section, which contains step-by-step instructions for initial setup, including screenshots or diagrams where applicable

steps.action: Navigate through each section sequentially by clicking 'Next' or the next section link
steps.expectedResult: Each section loads correctly with properly formatted text, images, code snippets, and callout boxes. Navigation between sections is smooth and consistent

steps.action: Verify that all images and diagrams within the user guide load correctly
steps.expectedResult: All images display properly with appropriate alt text, no broken image icons, and diagrams are legible at default zoom level

steps.action: Check that all internal cross-reference links within the user guide point to valid sections
steps.expectedResult: Clicking any cross-reference link navigates to the correct section within the user guide without 404 errors or broken anchors

postconditions: User guide is fully navigable and all sections are accessible
User remains on the documentation portal with session intact
All cross-reference links have been validated as functional

functional.title: Verify API endpoint documentation includes complete request and response examples
preconditions: User is on the API documentation page
At least 3 API endpoints are documented (e.g., GET, POST, PUT/PATCH, DELETE)
User has 'Developer' role or higher permissions
API documentation follows OpenAPI/Swagger specification or equivalent standard

steps.action: Navigate to the 'Endpoints' section of the API documentation and select the first listed endpoint (e.g., 'GET /api/v1/resources')
steps.expectedResult: The endpoint detail page displays: HTTP method, URL path, description, required/optional parameters, request headers, and authentication requirements

steps.action: Review the 'Request' section of the endpoint documentation
steps.expectedResult: The request section includes: complete URL with path parameters, query parameters with data types and descriptions, request headers (including Authorization), and a sample request body (for POST/PUT) in JSON format with proper syntax highlighting

steps.action: Review the 'Response' section of the endpoint documentation
steps.expectedResult: The response section includes: HTTP status codes (200, 201, 400, 401, 403, 404, 500), response body examples in JSON format for each status code, and field descriptions with data types

steps.action: Navigate to a POST endpoint (e.g., 'POST /api/v1/resources') and verify the request body schema documentation
steps.expectedResult: The POST endpoint documentation shows a complete request body schema with required fields marked, data types specified, validation rules noted, and a complete JSON example that can be copied

steps.action: Click the 'Copy' button next to a code example (request or response)
steps.expectedResult: The code example is copied to the clipboard, and a brief 'Copied!' tooltip or notification appears confirming the action

steps.action: Verify that error response examples are documented for at least 400, 401, 403, and 500 status codes
steps.expectedResult: Each error status code has a corresponding response body example showing the error message format, error code, and description fields

postconditions: All endpoint documentation pages have been verified to contain complete request/response examples
Code examples are copyable and properly formatted
Error responses are documented for all standard HTTP error codes

functional.title: Verify API authentication documentation is complete and accurate
preconditions: User is on the API documentation page
Authentication section exists in the API documentation
The API uses at least one authentication method (e.g., API key, OAuth 2.0, JWT)

steps.action: Navigate to the 'Authentication' section of the API documentation
steps.expectedResult: The Authentication section loads and clearly describes the supported authentication method(s) with an overview paragraph

steps.action: Review the authentication flow documentation for the primary authentication method
steps.expectedResult: A step-by-step authentication flow is documented, including: how to obtain credentials (API key or tokens), where to include credentials in requests (header, query parameter), token format and expiration details, and a complete authentication request example

steps.action: Verify that a sample authenticated request is provided with the correct Authorization header format
steps.expectedResult: A complete cURL or HTTP request example is shown with the Authorization header properly formatted (e.g., 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' or 'X-API-Key: <key>'), and the example is copyable

steps.action: Check that token refresh or renewal procedures are documented (if applicable)
steps.expectedResult: Token refresh documentation includes: refresh endpoint URL, request format, response format with new token, and handling of expired refresh tokens

steps.action: Verify that authentication error responses are documented (401 Unauthorized, 403 Forbidden)
steps.expectedResult: Authentication error scenarios are clearly documented with example error response bodies, common causes, and troubleshooting steps

postconditions: Authentication documentation is complete and provides all information needed for a developer to authenticate API requests
Sample requests are accurate and match the actual API authentication requirements
Error handling for authentication failures is clearly documented

functional.title: Verify search functionality within the documentation portal
preconditions: User is on the documentation portal (API docs or user guide)
Search functionality is available on the documentation page
Documentation contains at least 10 pages of content across multiple sections

steps.action: Locate the search bar on the documentation page (typically in the top navigation or sidebar)
steps.expectedResult: A search input field is visible with a placeholder text such as 'Search documentation...' and a search icon

steps.action: Type 'authentication' into the search bar and press Enter or click the search icon
steps.expectedResult: Search results appear within 2 seconds, displaying a list of relevant documentation pages/sections that contain the term 'authentication', with page titles, brief excerpts with the search term highlighted, and section paths

steps.action: Click on the first search result
steps.expectedResult: The user is navigated to the correct documentation page/section, and the search term is highlighted or the page scrolls to the relevant content

steps.action: Return to the search results and type a specific API endpoint path (e.g., '/api/v1/users') into the search bar
steps.expectedResult: Search results display the specific endpoint documentation page as the top result, along with any other pages that reference this endpoint

steps.action: Clear the search bar and type a term that does not exist in the documentation (e.g., 'xyznonexistent123')
steps.expectedResult: A 'No results found' message is displayed with a suggestion to try different keywords or browse the table of contents

postconditions: Search functionality returns accurate and relevant results for valid queries
Search results link to the correct documentation sections
No results scenario is handled gracefully with helpful messaging

functional.title: Verify documentation navigation and table of contents functionality
preconditions: User is on the documentation portal
Documentation has a sidebar or table of contents navigation
Documentation contains multiple sections and sub-sections (at least 3 levels deep)

steps.action: Observe the sidebar or table of contents navigation panel on the documentation page
steps.expectedResult: A structured navigation panel is visible showing all top-level sections with expandable/collapsible sub-sections indicated by arrow icons or +/- indicators

steps.action: Click on a top-level section header that has sub-sections (e.g., 'API Endpoints')
steps.expectedResult: The section expands to reveal sub-sections (e.g., 'Users', 'Resources', 'Settings'), and the section header is visually highlighted as the current active section

steps.action: Click on a sub-section item (e.g., 'Users' under 'API Endpoints')
steps.expectedResult: The main content area updates to display the selected sub-section content, and the navigation item is highlighted/bolded to indicate the current location

steps.action: Scroll down within the content area and observe the navigation panel behavior
steps.expectedResult: The navigation panel either remains fixed/sticky on the side or the current section indicator updates as the user scrolls through content, providing clear context of the user's position

steps.action: Click the 'Back to top' link or the documentation home/overview link
steps.expectedResult: The page scrolls to the top or navigates to the documentation landing page, and the navigation panel resets to show the top-level view

steps.action: Use the browser's back button after navigating through 3-4 documentation sections
steps.expectedResult: The browser navigates back through the previously visited documentation sections in the correct order, with the navigation panel updating to reflect the current section

postconditions: Navigation panel accurately reflects the documentation structure
Current section is always clearly indicated in the navigation
Browser history is properly maintained for documentation navigation

functional.title: Verify API documentation includes rate limiting and usage information
preconditions: User is on the API documentation page
Rate limiting section exists in the API documentation
API has defined rate limits for at least one tier or endpoint

steps.action: Navigate to the 'Rate Limiting' or 'Usage Limits' section of the API documentation
steps.expectedResult: The rate limiting section loads and displays a clear overview of the API rate limiting policy

steps.action: Review the rate limit details for the default/standard tier
steps.expectedResult: The documentation specifies: requests per minute/hour/day limits, rate limit headers returned in API responses (e.g., X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset), and the HTTP status code returned when limits are exceeded (429 Too Many Requests)

steps.action: Check for documentation on rate limit response headers
steps.expectedResult: A table or list describes each rate limit header with its name, description, data type, and an example value

steps.action: Verify that the 429 error response body is documented with an example
steps.expectedResult: A sample 429 response body is shown in JSON format including an error message, retry-after value, and any additional context about when the limit resets

postconditions: Rate limiting documentation provides all necessary information for developers to handle rate limits programmatically
Rate limit headers and error responses are clearly documented with examples

functional.title: Verify user guide Getting Started section provides complete onboarding flow
preconditions: User is on the User Guide documentation page
Getting Started section is available in the user guide
User is a new user or simulating a new user experience

steps.action: Navigate to the 'Getting Started' section of the user guide
steps.expectedResult: The Getting Started section loads with a clear introduction explaining the purpose of the guide and what the user will accomplish by following it

steps.action: Review Step 1 of the Getting Started guide (typically account creation or initial login)
steps.expectedResult: Step 1 provides clear instructions with screenshots showing the exact UI elements to interact with, including field labels, button names, and expected screen states

steps.action: Follow each subsequent step in the Getting Started guide, verifying that instructions match the actual application UI
steps.expectedResult: Each step accurately describes the current application UI, with screenshots that match the current version of the application, and instructions that lead to the expected outcomes

steps.action: Verify that the Getting Started guide includes prerequisites or system requirements
steps.expectedResult: A prerequisites section lists: supported browsers, required permissions/roles, any software dependencies, and minimum system requirements

steps.action: Check that the Getting Started guide concludes with a summary and next steps
steps.expectedResult: The guide ends with a summary of what was accomplished, links to more advanced sections of the user guide, and suggestions for next steps (e.g., 'Now that you have set up your account, learn how to configure your first project')

steps.action: Verify that all links within the Getting Started section to other documentation sections are functional
steps.expectedResult: All internal links navigate to the correct sections without 404 errors, and external links (if any) open in a new tab and point to valid resources

postconditions: Getting Started guide provides a complete, accurate onboarding experience
All screenshots and UI references match the current application version
All links within the section are functional and point to correct destinations

functional.title: Verify documentation version selector and versioned content display
preconditions: User is on the documentation portal
Multiple API/documentation versions are available (e.g., v1.0, v2.0)
Version selector dropdown or toggle is present on the documentation page

steps.action: Locate the version selector on the documentation page (typically a dropdown in the header or sidebar)
steps.expectedResult: A version selector is visible showing the current documentation version (e.g., 'v2.0 (Latest)') with a dropdown indicator

steps.action: Click on the version selector dropdown
steps.expectedResult: A dropdown menu appears listing all available documentation versions (e.g., 'v2.0 (Latest)', 'v1.0') with the current version highlighted or checked

steps.action: Select an older version (e.g., 'v1.0') from the dropdown
steps.expectedResult: The documentation content updates to display the v1.0 version, the version selector shows 'v1.0' as the current selection, and a banner or notice may appear indicating the user is viewing an older version with a link to the latest

steps.action: Navigate to a specific endpoint or section within the older version documentation
steps.expectedResult: The content displayed is specific to the selected version, showing endpoints, parameters, and examples that correspond to v1.0 of the API

steps.action: Switch back to the latest version using the version selector or the 'View latest version' banner link
steps.expectedResult: The documentation updates to the latest version content, the version selector reflects the latest version, and any version warning banner is removed

postconditions: Version switching works correctly and displays version-appropriate content
Users are clearly informed when viewing an older version of the documentation
The URL may reflect the selected version for bookmarking purposes

functional.title: Verify interactive API playground or 'Try It Out' functionality
preconditions: User is on the API documentation page for a specific endpoint
Interactive API playground or 'Try It Out' feature is available
User has valid API credentials or a sandbox/test environment is configured
User has 'Developer' role permissions

steps.action: Navigate to a GET endpoint documentation page (e.g., 'GET /api/v1/resources') and locate the 'Try It Out' or 'Send Request' button
steps.expectedResult: A 'Try It Out' button or interactive request panel is visible on the endpoint documentation page

steps.action: Click the 'Try It Out' button
steps.expectedResult: An interactive form appears with editable fields for: path parameters, query parameters, request headers (pre-filled with Authorization if authenticated), and request body (for POST/PUT endpoints)

steps.action: Fill in any required parameters with valid test values and click the 'Execute' or 'Send' button
steps.expectedResult: The API request is sent, and the response is displayed below showing: HTTP status code, response headers, response body in formatted JSON, and the actual cURL command that was executed

steps.action: Review the response section for completeness
steps.expectedResult: The response displays the status code with a color indicator (green for 2xx, red for 4xx/5xx), formatted and syntax-highlighted JSON response body, response time in milliseconds, and response headers

steps.action: Copy the generated cURL command from the 'Try It Out' response
steps.expectedResult: The cURL command is copied to the clipboard and can be pasted into a terminal to reproduce the exact same API request

postconditions: Interactive API playground successfully sends requests and displays responses
Generated cURL commands are accurate and reproducible
User credentials are not exposed in the documentation UI beyond the necessary authorization header

functional.title: Verify documentation PDF/print export functionality
preconditions: User is on the documentation portal (API docs or user guide)
Export or print functionality is available
User's browser supports PDF generation or print dialog

steps.action: Locate the 'Export' or 'Download PDF' or 'Print' button on the documentation page
steps.expectedResult: An export/download/print button or link is visible, typically in the page header or as a floating action button

steps.action: Click the 'Download PDF' or 'Export' button
steps.expectedResult: A PDF file is generated and downloaded to the user's default download location, or a print dialog opens with a print-optimized view of the documentation

steps.action: Open the downloaded PDF file and verify its contents
steps.expectedResult: The PDF contains all documentation content with proper formatting, including: table of contents with page numbers, all text content, code examples with formatting preserved, images and diagrams, and page headers/footers with document title and page numbers

steps.action: Verify that the PDF table of contents links work (if applicable)
steps.expectedResult: Clicking on table of contents entries in the PDF navigates to the correct page within the document

postconditions: PDF export contains complete and properly formatted documentation
Downloaded file is a valid PDF that opens in standard PDF readers
No sensitive information (API keys, tokens) is included in the exported document

functional.title: Verify documentation code examples are available in multiple programming languages
preconditions: User is on the API documentation page for a specific endpoint
Code examples section is available with language selector tabs
At least 3 programming languages are supported (e.g., cURL, Python, JavaScript, Java)

steps.action: Navigate to an API endpoint documentation page and locate the code examples section
steps.expectedResult: A code examples section is displayed with language selector tabs (e.g., 'cURL', 'Python', 'JavaScript', 'Java', 'C#') above a code block

steps.action: Click on the 'cURL' tab
steps.expectedResult: A complete cURL command example is displayed with proper syntax highlighting, including the full URL, HTTP method, headers, and request body (if applicable)

steps.action: Click on the 'Python' tab
steps.expectedResult: A complete Python code example is displayed using a common HTTP library (e.g., requests), with proper syntax highlighting, import statements, and comments explaining key parts

steps.action: Click on the 'JavaScript' tab
steps.expectedResult: A complete JavaScript code example is displayed using fetch API or axios, with proper syntax highlighting, async/await patterns, and error handling

steps.action: Click the 'Copy' button on any code example
steps.expectedResult: The entire code example is copied to the clipboard with a 'Copied!' confirmation, and the copied code maintains proper formatting when pasted into a text editor

steps.action: Verify that each code example includes proper error handling and comments
steps.expectedResult: Each language example includes try/catch or equivalent error handling, inline comments explaining the request structure, and placeholder values clearly marked (e.g., '<YOUR_API_KEY>')

postconditions: Code examples are available and syntactically correct for all supported languages
Language selection persists when navigating between endpoint pages (if applicable)
Copied code examples are ready to use with minimal modification (only replacing placeholder values)

functional.title: Verify user guide troubleshooting section covers common issues
preconditions: User is on the User Guide documentation page
Troubleshooting section exists in the user guide
At least 5 common issues are documented

steps.action: Navigate to the 'Troubleshooting' section of the user guide
steps.expectedResult: The Troubleshooting section loads with a list of common issues organized by category (e.g., Authentication Issues, Configuration Errors, Performance Problems)

steps.action: Click on the first troubleshooting item (e.g., 'Unable to authenticate')
steps.expectedResult: The issue detail expands or navigates to show: a clear problem description, possible causes listed as bullet points, step-by-step resolution instructions, and links to related documentation sections

steps.action: Verify that each troubleshooting entry includes a 'Symptoms' or 'Problem' description
steps.expectedResult: Each entry clearly describes what the user would experience (e.g., 'You receive a 401 Unauthorized error when making API requests') so users can identify if this matches their issue

steps.action: Check that resolution steps are actionable and specific
steps.expectedResult: Resolution steps include specific actions (e.g., 'Navigate to Settings > API Keys and verify your key has not expired'), not vague instructions like 'check your configuration'

steps.action: Verify that a 'Contact Support' or 'Still need help?' section exists at the bottom of the troubleshooting page
steps.expectedResult: A support contact section is present with: support email address or link, support ticket submission form or link, expected response time, and information to include when contacting support

postconditions: Troubleshooting section covers the most common user issues with actionable resolution steps
Users have a clear escalation path if self-service troubleshooting does not resolve their issue
All links within troubleshooting entries point to valid documentation sections

functional.title: Verify documentation breadcrumb navigation and URL structure
preconditions: User is on the documentation portal
Documentation has a hierarchical structure with at least 3 levels
Breadcrumb navigation is implemented on documentation pages

steps.action: Navigate to a deeply nested documentation page (e.g., API Docs > Endpoints > Users > GET /users)
steps.expectedResult: A breadcrumb trail is displayed at the top of the content area showing the full navigation path: 'Home > API Documentation > Endpoints > Users > GET /users'

steps.action: Click on the 'Endpoints' breadcrumb link
steps.expectedResult: The user is navigated to the Endpoints overview page, and the breadcrumb updates to show 'Home > API Documentation > Endpoints'

steps.action: Verify the URL structure reflects the documentation hierarchy
steps.expectedResult: The browser URL shows a clean, readable path (e.g., '/docs/api/endpoints' or '/docs/api/endpoints/users/get') that can be bookmarked and shared

steps.action: Copy the current documentation page URL and open it in a new browser tab
steps.expectedResult: The exact same documentation page loads in the new tab, confirming that documentation URLs are deep-linkable and shareable

steps.action: Click the 'Home' breadcrumb link
steps.expectedResult: The user is navigated back to the documentation portal landing page with the full table of contents visible

postconditions: Breadcrumb navigation accurately reflects the user's position in the documentation hierarchy
Documentation URLs are clean, readable, and deep-linkable
Shared documentation URLs load the correct page for other users

functional.title: Verify documentation renders correctly on mobile devices
preconditions: User has access to a mobile device or browser developer tools with mobile emulation
Documentation portal is expected to be responsive
Testing on at least two viewport sizes: mobile (375px width) and tablet (768px width)

steps.action: Open the documentation portal on a mobile device (or set browser to 375px width mobile emulation) and navigate to the API documentation landing page
steps.expectedResult: The documentation page renders in a mobile-friendly layout with: readable text without horizontal scrolling, a hamburger menu or collapsible navigation replacing the sidebar, and properly scaled images

steps.action: Tap the hamburger menu or navigation toggle to access the table of contents
steps.expectedResult: A mobile navigation panel slides in or expands, showing the full table of contents with touch-friendly tap targets (at least 44x44px)

steps.action: Navigate to an API endpoint page and verify code examples display correctly
steps.expectedResult: Code examples are displayed in a scrollable container that allows horizontal scrolling for long lines, with syntax highlighting preserved and copy buttons accessible

steps.action: Switch to tablet viewport (768px width) and verify the layout adjusts appropriately
steps.expectedResult: The documentation layout adjusts to show a condensed sidebar or top navigation, with content area utilizing the available width effectively

steps.action: Test pinch-to-zoom on a diagram or image within the documentation
steps.expectedResult: Images and diagrams can be zoomed in for detail, and the page layout does not break when zooming

postconditions: Documentation is fully readable and navigable on mobile and tablet devices
No content is cut off or inaccessible on smaller viewports
Code examples remain usable with horizontal scrolling on mobile

functional.title: Verify API documentation error codes reference section is complete
preconditions: User is on the API documentation page
An 'Error Codes' or 'Error Reference' section exists in the documentation
The API returns structured error responses

steps.action: Navigate to the 'Error Codes' or 'Error Reference' section of the API documentation
steps.expectedResult: A comprehensive error codes reference page loads with a table or list of all possible API error codes

steps.action: Verify the error codes table includes columns for: HTTP Status Code, Error Code, Error Message, and Description
steps.expectedResult: A well-structured table displays all error codes with the four required columns, sorted by HTTP status code or error code

steps.action: Check that standard HTTP error codes are documented: 400, 401, 403, 404, 409, 422, 429, 500, 502, 503
steps.expectedResult: All standard HTTP error codes that the API may return are listed with specific descriptions of when each code is returned in the context of this API

steps.action: Verify that custom/application-specific error codes are documented (if applicable)
steps.expectedResult: Any custom error codes (e.g., 'INVALID_FIELD_FORMAT', 'RESOURCE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED') are listed with clear descriptions, the HTTP status code they accompany, and example scenarios

steps.action: Check that a sample error response body structure is provided
steps.expectedResult: A generic error response body example is shown in JSON format (e.g., {"error": {"code": "INVALID_REQUEST", "message": "The request body is missing required field 'name'", "details": [...]}}) with field descriptions

postconditions: Error codes reference is complete and covers all possible API error responses
Developers can use the error reference to programmatically handle all error scenarios
Error response format is consistent and well-documented

functional.title: Verify documentation feedback mechanism allows users to rate and comment on pages
preconditions: User is on any documentation page (API docs or user guide)
A feedback mechanism (thumbs up/down, rating, or comment form) is present on documentation pages
User is logged in

steps.action: Scroll to the bottom of a documentation page and locate the feedback section (e.g., 'Was this page helpful?' with thumbs up/down buttons)
steps.expectedResult: A feedback section is visible at the bottom of the page with a question like 'Was this page helpful?' and interactive feedback options (thumbs up/down, star rating, or similar)

steps.action: Click the 'Yes' or thumbs up button to indicate the page was helpful
steps.expectedResult: The button state changes to indicate the selection (e.g., highlighted or filled), and a brief 'Thank you for your feedback!' message appears

steps.action: If a comment/suggestion text field appears after rating, enter 'Great documentation, very clear examples.' and click 'Submit'
steps.expectedResult: The comment is submitted successfully with a confirmation message like 'Your feedback has been submitted. Thank you!'

steps.action: Navigate to a different documentation page and verify the feedback section resets
steps.expectedResult: The feedback section on the new page shows unselected/default state, allowing the user to provide independent feedback for this page

postconditions: User feedback is recorded and associated with the specific documentation page
Feedback submission does not disrupt the user's documentation browsing experience
Users can provide feedback on multiple pages independently

functional.title: Verify documentation changelog or release notes section tracks API changes
preconditions: User is on the documentation portal
A 'Changelog', 'Release Notes', or 'What's New' section exists
At least 2 versions of changes are documented

steps.action: Navigate to the 'Changelog' or 'Release Notes' section of the documentation
steps.expectedResult: The changelog page loads with entries organized in reverse chronological order (newest first), each entry showing a date, version number, and summary of changes

steps.action: Review the most recent changelog entry
steps.expectedResult: The entry includes: release date, version number, categorized changes (e.g., 'New Features', 'Bug Fixes', 'Breaking Changes', 'Deprecations'), and brief descriptions of each change with links to relevant documentation sections

steps.action: Check for 'Breaking Changes' or 'Migration Guide' sections in changelog entries
steps.expectedResult: Any breaking changes are clearly highlighted (e.g., with a warning icon or red label) and include migration instructions or links to a migration guide

steps.action: Click on a link within a changelog entry that references updated documentation
steps.expectedResult: The link navigates to the correct, updated documentation section showing the changes described in the changelog entry

steps.action: Verify that deprecated features or endpoints are clearly marked in the changelog
steps.expectedResult: Deprecated items include: the deprecation date, the planned removal date, the recommended alternative, and a link to the migration guide

postconditions: Changelog provides a complete history of API and documentation changes
Breaking changes and deprecations are prominently highlighted
All links within changelog entries navigate to correct documentation sections
